question: Does a short Cirrove-owned Secret Service key plus an authenticated encrypted iCloud session in private account state survive the keyring-file transition and a delayed isolated-service restart that previously failed for the large direct keyring value?
arms: fresh foreground iCloud re-sign-in on the isolated account
key length, sealed-file size and permissions immediately after sign-in
metadata-only key and file checks through at least 30 minutes while the isolated service runs
clean isolated-service restart, then mount status, root listing and one owned test-file read
endpoint: The short key remains nonempty, the sealed file remains private and authenticated, and the isolated service reaches ready after restart without another sign-in. Record only lengths, file mode, timestamps, counts and outcome; never secret values, account identifiers, raw provider bodies, URLs or file contents.
prediction: The short key will outlast 30 minutes and a keyring-file write, so the new service will restore the sealed session after restart. This is a directional prediction, not proof of Apple-session longevity or a known keyring root cause.
scope: Only the isolated iCloud validation state and its read-only mount; the regular Cirrove service and other cloud mounts are excluded.

results.note: The post-sign-in monitor ran from 17:50 to 18:04 UTC and sampled at 20-second intervals, writing only changed records or five-minute heartbeats. Earlier key length was checked after sign-in but not continuously sampled; the record therefore establishes retained values at observations, not an uninterrupted trace.

interpretation: The short-key plus sealed-file path survived one delayed restart where the preceding direct large-keyring sessions had failed. This is one account and one run. It does not establish the cause of the original keyring loss, repeatability, expiry renewal or broad iCloud reliability.
